title: Add an inverse-XFAIL verdict: LRM requires ACCEPTANCE, VerA rejects
detail: BLOCKS ch05-02..ch05-09. README.md defines `//! xfail` as 'the LRM says the construct is an error, the fixture demands the diagnostic, and VerA does not produce it yet'. Eight ch05 fixtures are the exact inverse: the LRM REQUIRES the construct and VerA rejects it. There is no verdict for that, so today they are written as `//! reject` of legal source, which is why a conforming compiler FAILS the suite. Needs a third verdict alongside CANNOT RUN and XFAIL (proposed `//! unsupported <reason>` next to a `//! reject`), counted, not a pass, and failing under --strict, with the same XPASS-is-a-hard-FAIL rule so the day VerA accepts the construct the fixture demands conversion to a positive.
expected: A verdict that records 'VerA rejects what the LRM requires' without asserting the rejection is correct; README.md section added next to 'Known gap — the XFAIL verdict'.

title: generic_access.va demands rejection of the generic potential()/flow() access functions 5.5.1 requires
detail: Verified in ch5-analog.html Syntax 5-3: `nature_access_function ::= nature_attribute_identifier | potential | flow`, and 5.5.1's measure1 example writes `potential(p) / V` verbatim. The fixture is `//! reject expression` on `analog potential(p) <+ flow(p) * 25.0;`. A conforming compiler accepts this and FAILS the fixture; VerA passes it by having the gap. COVERAGE.md compounds it by listing generic_access.va as the fixture that COVERS 5.5.1.
expected: Either a positive fixture asserting potential()/flow() equal V()/I() on the same branch, or `//! lrm 5.5.1` + `//! reject` + the new unsupported verdict from ch05-01.

title: vector_access.va demands rejection of vector element selection, which 5.5.2 requires
detail: 5.5.2 verbatim: 'The scalar element of a vector is selected with an index, e.g., V(in[1]) accesses the voltage in[1].' The clause then prints two worked examples (the N-bit DAC and DAC8) built entirely on V(in[i]). The fixture is `//! reject identifier` on `I(p[0]) <+ V(p[1]);`. Legal source, demanded rejection.
expected: `//! lrm 5.5.2` + unsupported verdict; converted to a positive DAC8-style bit-weighting fixture when VerA supports vector nets.

title: analog_genvar_loop.va demands rejection of the analog_for the 5.9.3 example itself writes
detail: 5.9.3's genvarexp example is `genvar k; ... for (k = 1; k <= width; k = k + 1) begin tmp = tmp + V(dt[k]); V(out) <+ ddt(V(dt[k])); end` inside an analog block. The fixture writes the same construct and asserts `//! reject identifier`. Also note COVERAGE.md maps 5.9.3 to this file, so the chapter's only claim on analog_for coverage is a rejection of it.
expected: `//! lrm 5.9.3` + unsupported verdict; the LRM's own genvarexp as the eventual positive.

title: nature_attribute_unsupported.va demands rejection of the 5.5.3 twocap example verbatim
detail: 5.5.3's only example is `I(a,b) <+ c*ddt(V(a,b), a.potential.abstol);`. The fixture is `analog I(p) <+ ddt(V(p), p.potential.abstol);` with `//! reject expected `)``. The expectation is also a bare parser-message substring that pins nothing (see ch05-40).
expected: `//! lrm 5.5.3` + unsupported verdict. Note 5.5.3 also bans this syntax for access/ddt_nature/idt_nature — that is a separate REAL negative, see ch05-33.

title: hierarchical_access_unsupported.va rejects hierarchical net access 5.5.4 requires, and rejects it for the wrong reason
detail: 5.5.4's signal_monitor example probes `V(top.drv.a)` and `V(top.drv.a, top.drv.b)` with NO module instantiation anywhere. The fixture adds `child u(p);` purely to reach a 'module instantiation is not supported' diagnostic, so its asserted message is about a ch06 construct, not about 5.5.4 at all. Both wrong: legal source, and an expectation aimed at a different rule.
expected: Drop the `child u(p);` instance, keep the bare hierarchical probe, `//! lrm 5.5.4` + unsupported verdict.

title: hierarchical_contribution_unsupported.va rejects the 5.6.8.1 hierarchical contribution, masked by a module-instantiation error
detail: Same defect as ch05-06 on the contribution side: `analog I(u.internal) <+ 1m;` plus a `child u(p);` instance whose diagnostic is the one actually asserted. COVERAGE.md already concedes this in prose ('source inventory only, with the asserted failure at module instantiation') rather than fixing it.
expected: Drop the instance, `//! lrm 5.6.8.1` + unsupported verdict.

title: named_event_unsupported.va is self-declared DEBT: it demands rejection of legal 5.10.4 named events
detail: The file's own 30-line header argues at length that named events ARE in the Verilog-A subset and that 'the fixture's own header comment is wrong'. It asserts `//! reject ParseError` + `//! reject E0203`. Worse, it is the ONLY file in the tree containing a contribution inside an event control block — the 5.10 prohibition VerA already diagnoses as E0406 — and its own comment admits E0406 'is simply not the first diagnostic here', so that rule is untested tree-wide (see ch05-22).
expected: Split: `//! lrm 5.10.4` + unsupported verdict for the named event, and a separate clean E0406 fixture.

title: analog_initial_digital_access_rejected.va pins a diagnostic about legal Verilog-AMS syntax, not 5.2.1's digital-access ban
detail: The fixture asserts `//! reject E0205` + `reg` + `initial` — i.e. it pins VerA's refusal of `reg` and the digital `initial` block, which are legal Verilog-AMS. A conforming AMS compiler fails it; a Verilog-A-only compiler passes it without ever implementing 5.2.1's rule that digital values cannot be read from an analog initial block. COVERAGE.md's own 'Parser-boundary disclosure' admits the analog rule is never reached.
expected: Rewrite so the analog-initial digital read is the FIRST diagnostic, `//! lrm 5.2.1`; or split the annex-C `reg`/`initial` rejection into its own ch07/annex-C fixture.

title: absdelta_digital_only.va carries a false DEBT header — VerA's rejection is exactly what 5.10.3.4 requires
detail: The inverse error to ch05-02..09. 5.10.3.4 verbatim: 'This function is only allowed in an initial or always block of a Verilog-AMS module.' The fixture puts `@(absdelta(V(p), 1p))` in an ANALOG block, so E0513 is correct conformance. Its header nonetheless says 'DEBT — this rejection is NOT conformance. The LRM permits what VerA refuses here' and says `zig build ledger` counts the rule against VerA. That charges VerA with a defect it does not have and marks a correct fixture for deletion.
expected: Strip the DEBT header, add `//! lrm 5.10.3.4`, keep `//! reject E0513`. Remove it from the ledger's debt count.

title: final_step.va asserts the value an unfired event also leaves, so it cannot test Table 5-1 at all
detail: Body is `@(final_step) x = 0.0;` and the check is `x == 0.0`. 0.0 is also what ch3 3.2 gives an untouched real, so the fixture passes identically whether final_step fires, never fires, or is not implemented. Its own header concedes 'the firing itself leaves no trace'. Table 5-1 gives final_step the value 1 at DCOP, which is the rule the file claims to pin. Reported independently by all three of uncovered, weak and literals.
expected: Assign a non-default sentinel in the event body (`x = 1.0`) and assert 1.0, so a compiler that drops final_step reads 0.0 and fails.

title: multiple_indirect.va aims two equations at one branch — a system 5.6.7.1 never defines — and its wants re-derive the bias
detail: The file writes `V(p,n) : V(c1) == V(p,n);` and `V(p,n) : V(c2) == 2.0*V(p,n);` — two indirect statements targeting the SAME branch, an over-determined system in one unknown. 5.6.7.1's example is three equations across three DISTINCT targets (V(x), V(y), V(z)), and its point is that targets can be paired with equations in any order. Separately, all three wants (0.0, 0.0, 0.0) follow from the `//! bias` lines alone: delete both `:` statements and every ok=1 still stands.
expected: Two distinct branch targets following 5.6.7.1's shape, with at least one want that only the solved system produces.

title: indirect_contribution.va's wants are the declared bias, not the solution of the constraint
detail: Wants are V(p,n)==0.75 and V(ctrl)-2*V(p,n)==0.0. `//! bias` already declares V(ctrl)=1.5, V(p)=0.75, V(n)=0.0, so both are pure arithmetic over the harness inputs. Delete the `V(p,n) : V(ctrl) == 2.0*V(p,n);` statement and the fixture still prints ok=1 twice — the indirect contribution is not under test.
expected: An operating point the harness does NOT pin to the solution, so the asserted value can only come from the solver honouring the constraint.

title: implicit_zero_contribution.va and retained_conditional_contribution.va assert 4.2.5 arithmetic, never 5.6.1.3 retention
detail: implicit_zero_contribution.va's checks reduce to `1*0.5==0.5` and `0*0.5==0.0`; retained_conditional_contribution.va's to `1*1m==1e-3` and `0*1m==0.0`. Both are relational-operator-is-an-integer facts from 4.2.5 multiplied by a bias, evaluated with the contribution statement playing no part. Neither observes the retained branch value. Both files nonetheless head themselves '5.6.1.3 value retention', and COVERAGE.md maps 5.6.1–5.6.1.3 to retained_conditional_contribution.va. Also applies to switch_branch.va and unassigned_switch_arm.va.
expected: Either an oracle that reads the retained source value, or honest headers scoping them to 5.4.4/5.6.5 with 5.6.1.3 left to ch05-34.

title: No fixture in the chapter ever observes a cross() event firing — a compiler with no cross() passes all four
detail: event_cross.va, event_cross_any.va, event_cross_falling.va and event_cross_enable.va all assert that the sampled variable is still 0.0, i.e. that nothing happened. Three of them are dc, where 5.10.3.1 bars the event outright, so they are true by the clause regardless of implementation. Nothing anywhere asserts the positive half of the rule.
expected: A transient fixture whose `//! wave` walks the expression through a rising zero crossing and asserts the sampled value the firing must produce.

title: event_timer_one_shot.va never runs past its own start_time, so it proves neither 'fires' nor 'only once'
detail: `@(timer(1n, 0.0)) x = 1.0;` with `//! time 0, 0.25n, 0.5n, 0.75n` — every declared timepoint is strictly before t=1n. The fixture asserts x==0.0, which is the 3.2 default. The file's own header concedes 'the one-shot half of the rule is not observable from inside this module'. The rule it is named for (period<=0 makes the timer fire exactly once) is untested.
expected: Extend `//! time` past 1n and count firings into an integer, so one firing reads 1 and a repeating timer reads more.

title: two_named_branches.va passes unchanged on a compiler that collapses the two branch declarations
detail: Both branches span the same net pair and both asserts are V(...)==0.5, which is the node difference either way. The stated claim — 'a compiler that collapsed the two declarations misses one of them' — is exactly what the assertions cannot detect, because a collapsed single branch still reads 0.5 for both names.
expected: Give the two branches different contributed values and assert something that differs when they are merged (e.g. the flow through each).

title: event_above.va and event_above_tolerance.va require an above() event in a standalone dc OP, which no 'shall' sentence grants
detail: 5.10.3.2's two normative sentences are (a) 'If the expression is positive at the conclusion of the initial condition analysis that precedes a TRANSIENT analysis, the above() function shall generate an event' and (b) 'During a DC SWEEP, the above() function shall also generate an event when the expression crosses zero from below.' Both fixtures use a single-point dc operating point with a constantly-positive expression, which is neither case; they lean on the permissive 'but the above() function can'. Demoted from the lens's reading — the claim is over-specified rather than wrong.
expected: Restate as a dc sweep crossing zero from below, or as the initial condition preceding a transient — the two forms the clause actually mandates.

title: event_cross_enable.va carries a stale 'FAILS TODAY' defect note for a bug that is fixed
detail: The header states 'FAILS TODAY — known VerA defect... crossTest in src/backend/codegen.zig builds the hit test from args[0..1] only; the enable argument (args[4]) is never read, so a disabled cross() still fires.' Verified false: codegen.zig now has `enableTest`, and UnitPlan gives the enable argument a slot; `zig build torture -- ch05` reports 82/82 with this fixture passing. A stale defect note invites someone to 'fix' working code.
expected: Delete the FAILS TODAY paragraph; add `//! lrm 5.10.3.1`.

title: Three tolerances do not match the arithmetic they guard
detail: Recomputed in double precision. conductor.va: g*V = 0.001*0.6 is bit-exact against the 6.0e-4 want (0 ulp error) yet carries RTOL 1e-12, which is 5534 ulp of slack. constant_current_source.va: same, 1e-6 exact under RTOL 1e-12 = 4722 ulp. controlled_sources.va is the opposite — `3m*V(cp,cn)` has only 4.6x margin under its 1e-18 absolute tolerance, because 0.7-0.2 = 0.49999999999999994, giving 1.4999999999999998e-3 against a 1.5e-3 want. Nothing fails today and nothing is masked; the tolerances just do not describe the operation. Note the `weak` lens reported 'no over-loose tolerances found' — verified wrong, literals is right.
expected: CHECKX on the two exact products; either widen controlled_sources.va's tolerance to ~1e-17 or write the want as the exactly-produced 1.4999999999999998e-3.

title: No fixture anywhere puts a port access function on the left of `<+` — E0407 would fire and never does
detail: 5.4.3 verbatim: 'The port access function shall not be used on the left side of a contribution operator <+.' grep across the whole fixtures tree finds no `I(<...>) <+` anywhere. port_potential_invalid.va pins the OTHER 5.4.3 prohibition (V(<a>) is invalid, E0507); this one is untested. VerA already implements E0407, so the fixture passes on the day it is written.
expected:
`//! lrm 5.4.3` + `//! reject E0407` on `analog I(

) <+ 1m;`

title: Contribution inside an event control block has no clean fixture — E0406 is unprovoked tree-wide
detail: 5.10 verbatim: 'Contribution statements cannot be used inside an event control block because it can generate discontinuity in analog signals.' The only file in the tree containing the construct is named_event_unsupported.va, which rejects on its `event tick;` declaration first and admits so in its own comment. grep finds E0406 in zero .va files.
expected: `//! lrm 5.10` + `//! reject E0406` on `analog @(initial_step) I(p) <+ 1m;` — a global event, so no named-event parse error masks it.

title: Nested event control statements have no fixture — E0703 is unprovoked tree-wide
detail: 5.10's third bullet: 'Nested event control statements are not allowed.' Zero .va files in the tree mention E0703.
expected: `//! lrm 5.10` + `//! reject E0703` on `analog @(initial_step) @(final_step) x = 1.0;`

title: Indirect contribution under a conditional has no fixture — E0412 is unprovoked tree-wide
detail: 5.6.7 bans indirect contributions in conditional and looping statements unless the guard is constant. Zero .va files mention E0412.
expected: `//! lrm 5.6.7` + `//! reject E0412` on an indirect statement guarded by a runtime probe.

title: Illegal left-hand side of the `==` in an indirect contribution has no fixture — E0414 is unprovoked tree-wide
detail: Zero .va files mention E0414. diag_code.zig describes it as 'the mirror image of E0409'.

title: break/continue outside any loop has no fixture — E0404 is unprovoked tree-wide
detail: 5.11 verbatim: 'The continue and break statements can only be used in a loop.' Verified present in ch5-analog.html (Syntax 5-22) — see the DROPPED note on the literals lens. Zero .va files mention E0404.
expected: `//! lrm 5.11` + `//! reject E0404` on a bare `break;` in an analog block.

title: break/continue inside an analog_for has no fixture
detail: 5.11 verbatim: 'The continue and break statements cannot be used inside an analog for loop. Refer 5.9.3.' A distinct rule from ch05-26 — inside a loop, but the wrong kind of loop. No fixture in the tree.
expected: `//! lrm 5.11` + `//! lrm 5.9.3` + reject; may need the ch05-01 verdict or an xfail if VerA does not separate analog_for from a runtime for.

title: Two `default` items in one case statement — no fixture
detail: 5.8.3 verbatim: 'The default statement is optional. Use of multiple default statements in one case statement is illegal.' The chapter has case_statement.va and case_default_only.va, neither with a duplicate.
expected: `//! lrm 5.8.3` + reject on a case with two default arms.

title: None of 5.9's three blanket loop prohibitions has a reject fixture
detail: 5.9 verbatim, for repeat/while/non-genvar-for: 'Analog filter functions are not allowed / Event control statements are not allowed / Contribution statements are not allowed'. The chapter has repeat_loop.va, while_loop.va, for_loop.va, repeat_single.va, while_false.va, for_zero_iterations.va — six positives, zero negatives. Three fixtures needed (contribution / filter / event control); this item names the first, siblings loop_filter_invalid.va and loop_event_control_invalid.va.
expected: `//! lrm 5.9` + reject on each of the three, in a plain `while`/`repeat`.

title: Using both the potential AND the flow of a probe branch is illegal — no fixture
detail: 5.4.2.1 makes an unnamed branch appearing only on the right-hand side a probe, and fixes the complementary quantity at zero; using both is illegal. source_probe_both.va is a POSITIVE fixture about a source branch, not this rule.
expected: `//! lrm 5.4.2.1` + reject on a module reading both V(a,b) and I(a,b) of a probe-only branch.

title: Event control inside a conditional / case / repeat / while has no fixture
detail: 5.10.3.1's last 'shall': an event function 'shall not be used inside an if, case, casex, or casez statement unless the conditional expression is a genvar expression', reinforced by 5.8.4 and 5.9. No fixture in the chapter puts an `@(...)` under a condition.
expected: `//! lrm 5.8.4` + `//! lrm 5.10.3.1` + reject on `if (V(c) > 0) @(initial_step) x = 1.0;`

title: None of 5.7's assignment restrictions has a reject fixture
detail: 5.7 lists, verbatim: 'Concatenation expressions cannot be used as part of the analog_expression', 'Hierarchical assignment of a variable from another scope/module is not allowed', and for arrays 'Array assignments shall only be done with arrays that are compatible' (the LRM prints '// type check error' against its own example). The chapter's only 5.7 fixture is procedural_assignments.va, a positive. Three fixtures; this names the first, siblings assignment_hierarchical_invalid.va and assignment_array_mismatch_invalid.va.
expected: `//! lrm 5.7` + reject on each.

title: cross()/above()/timer()/absdelta() argument well-formedness is entirely untested
detail: Four constraints verified in ch5-analog.html 5.10.3.1: tolerances 'shall be non-negative'; 'The dir and enable arguments, if specified, shall evaluate to integers'; 'If either or both tolerances are defined, then the direction shall also be defined'; and 'Null arguments are not allowed in analog events' (5.10). Zero fixtures. IMPORTANT: do NOT write the two PDF-only sentences the negatives lens quoted — see the DROPPED note. Siblings: cross_tolerance_without_dir_invalid.va, event_null_argument_invalid.va. Also 5.5.3's ban on nature-attribute syntax for access/ddt_nature/idt_nature belongs here as nature_attribute_nonconstant_invalid.va.
expected: `//! lrm 5.10.3.1` + reject on each constraint separately.

title: The LRM's own worked value-retention example, answer 7.0, has no fixture anywhere in the tree
detail: 5.6.1.3 Example 2 prints the module and states the answer: V(p,n)<+1.0 (1 retained); I(p,n)<+2.0 (potential discarded, flow 2 retained); V(p,n)<+3.0 (flow discarded, potential 3 retained); V(p,n)<+4.0 (added to 3) => 'an assignment of 7.0 to the potential source'. Nothing in ch05 or the tree writes these four lines; the two files that head themselves 5.6.1.3 test the 5.4.4 unassigned arm instead (ch05-14). This is the most explicitly-numeric rule in the chapter.
expected: The four contributions verbatim with 7.0 as the want. Caveat from the uncovered lens, confirmed: the harness forces node voltages and does not solve, so the retained value is visible only in the residual dump — the fixture may need the dump promoted to an oracle. Write it regardless.

title: Dangling-else binding has no fixture and is the chapter's other fully-numeric rule
detail: 5.8.2: 'This is resolved by always associating the else with the closest previous if() which lacks an else', with two printed variants. Without begin-end and index<=0, neither arm runs and result keeps its initial value; with begin-end the else binds to the OUTER if and result becomes j. Two fixtures (sibling: dangling_else_begin_end.va) whose wants differ, which is the whole point.
expected: `//! lrm 5.8.2`, the LRM's own if/i/j/result shape, with a sentinel initial value so 'neither arm ran' is distinguishable.

title: Implicit (fixed-point) contribution — the target on its own right-hand side — has no ch05 fixture
detail: 5.6.6's example is `I(diode) <+ is*(limexp((V(diode) - r*I(diode))/$vt) - 1);` — 'Notice that I(diode) is found on both sides of the contribution operator.' COVERAGE.md maps 5.6.5-5.6.6 to implicit_zero_contribution.va, which despite the name never puts the target on its own RHS; it is a 5.4.4 unassigned-arm test. The construct does appear elsewhere in the tree (exhaustive/081_diode.va, ch04_expressions/25_limexp.va), so this is a chapter-coverage and COVERAGE.md-accuracy gap rather than a tree-wide one.
expected: `//! lrm 5.6.6` on the LRM's diode form, with a want derived from the fixed point.

title: The repeat/while count is evaluated once before the body runs — no fixture
detail: 5.9.1: 'The repeat and while expressions shall be evaluated once before the execution of any statement in order to determine the number of times, if any, the statements are executed.' repeat_loop.va and repeat_single.va use constant counts, so a per-iteration re-evaluation would be invisible.
expected: `//! lrm 5.9.1` with a count expression over a variable the body mutates; the iteration count must follow the original value.

title: Table 5-1 rows no fixture reads: initial_step with an unknown analysis name, final_step("ac"), sweep positions
detail: initial_step.va, final_step.va and initial_final_analysis_lists.va cover the common rows; the table's edge rows — an analysis identifier the simulator does not recognise, and the first/last-point semantics across a sweep — are unread.
expected: `//! lrm 5.10.2` with `//! sweep` so first and last points are distinguishable.

title: Zero of the 82 .va files carry a `//! lrm` cite
detail: Verified: `grep -l '^//! lrm' *.va` returns nothing across all 82 files, and `grep -l xfail` likewise. README.md makes the cite the mechanism behind `zig build torture -- --coverage`, so the chapter contributes nothing to the only mechanical backing a coverage claim has. Most files already name their clause in a prose comment, so this is largely a transcription. (Both lenses said '100'/'101 files'; the actual count is 82 .va + 16 sidecars + COVERAGE.md.)
expected: One or more `//! lrm` lines per fixture, taken from the section each file's header already cites.

title: Six reject fixtures state their expectation as a bare message substring that pins nothing
detail: generic_access.va (`expression`), vector_access.va (`identifier`), analog_genvar_loop.va (`identifier`), nature_attribute_unsupported.va (`expected `)``), hierarchical_access_unsupported.va and hierarchical_contribution_unsupported.va (`module instantiation is not supported`). README.md: 'Codes are the preferred form: they are stable... and they pin WHICH rule fired rather than how it happened to be worded.' `identifier` and `expression` would match a diagnostic about any unrelated construct. Overlaps ch05-02..07, which rewrite the same six files.
expected: A diagnostic CODE per fixture, or a phase label where no code exists.

title: 16 .expected-error.txt sidecars exist that README.md says must not
detail: README.md opens 'One runner, tests/torture.zig. No sidecar files. A fixture states its own expected behavior, in the file... there is no second file to drift out of step with it.' All 16 duplicate the `//! reject` lines already in their .va, and named_event_unsupported.expected-error.txt has already drifted into carrying a 25-line commentary the .va also carries.
expected: Delete all 16; the `//! reject` lines already in each .va are authoritative.

title: COVERAGE.md's preamble and six disposition rows describe a contract that no longer exists, three of them stale
detail: The preamble reads 'Every valid .va is paired with an exact .expected.zig dump; diagnostic cases use .expected-error.txt' — both mechanisms are gone under the current README. Six rows carry 'snapshots the current acceptance gap' / 'records the missing diagnostic' prose; three are stale as verified against diag_code.zig and a passing run: the four 5.2.1 rejects DO produce E0421/E0422/E0405/E0702, port_potential_invalid.va DOES produce E0507, and conditional_filter_invalid.va DOES pin E0514.
expected: Rewrite the preamble to the `//! reject` / `//! lrm` contract; delete the three stale disposition clauses.

title: COVERAGE.md claims coverage from two fixtures that do not provide it
detail: Row '5.5.1 | discipline and generic potential/flow access | generic_access.va' — that file DEMANDS REJECTION of the construct 5.5.1 requires (ch05-02), so the chapter's 5.5.1 claim rests on a rejection of 5.5.1. Row '5.6.5-5.6.6 | switch branches and implicit zero contribution | switch_branch.va, implicit_zero_contribution.va' — implicit_zero_contribution.va never puts the target on its own RHS, so 5.6.6 is unclaimed (ch05-36). The same pattern affects the 5.9.3 row (ch05-04) and the 5.11 row, which says the jump fixtures 'snapshot current acceptance without the normative jump semantics' when they in fact assert exactly the normative semantics (ch05-45).
expected: Remove the two false mappings; re-point them at ch05-02 and ch05-36 once written.

title: 25 files cite a clause that does not exist or states a different rule
detail: Verified against the LRM HTML. 13 files attribute the zero-initialization rule to 3.2.1 — the rule ('Integer variables whose values are assigned in an analog context default to an initial value of zero'; 'Real variables are initialized to zero') sits in 3.2 'Integer and real data types'; 3.2.1 is 'Output variables'. 7 files cite 3.3.1, which does not exist (ch3 has 3.3 'String data type' with no subsections). 2 files (repeat_loop.va, repeat_single.va) cite 5.7.2, which does not exist. 3 files (conductor.va, constant_current_source.va, conditional_no_else.va) cite 2.5.1 for scale factors; ch2 has 2.5 with no subsections. analog_initial_integer.va cites 4.2.1.1 in the wrong direction.
expected: Bulk sed 3.2.1->3.2, 3.3.1->3.2, 5.7.2->5.9.1, 2.5.1->2.5; fix 4.2.1.1 by hand. Do this WITH ch05-39 so each comment cite and its `//! lrm` line agree.

title: The two jump fixtures are correct and passing, but their names and COVERAGE.md row say the opposite
detail: jump_statement_unsupported.va and jump_continue_unsupported.va assert i==0 after a `break` on the first pass and acc==0+1+3==4 for a `continue` skipping i==2. Both are correct 5.11 semantics, both PASS today (82/82), and VerA implements both keywords. The `_unsupported` suffix is reserved in this directory for constructs VerA rejects, and COVERAGE.md says they 'snapshot current acceptance without the normative jump semantics' — the reverse of what they do. READ THE DROPPED NOTE FIRST: the literals lens asked for these to be converted to `//! reject ParseError` + xfail on the grounds that 5.11 does not exist. It does. Do not convert them.
expected: Rename to jump_break.va and jump_continue.va, add `//! lrm 5.11`, correct the COVERAGE.md row. Sibling: jump_continue_unsupported.va.
